root_cause.text: The option walker loops in xt_tcpudp and xt_dccp fail to check if the current position is the last byte before reading op[i+1] to determine the length of a multi-byte option, causing a one-byte out-of-bounds read when a non-single-byte option kind occupies the final byte.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "When the last byte of options is a non-single-byte option kind, walkers that advance with i += op[i + 1] ? : 1 can read op[i + 1] past the end of the option area." The patch adds an explicit `i == optlen - 1` check before dereferencing `op[i + 1]` in both xt_tcpudp and xt_dccp walkers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add boundary check to prevent out-of-bounds access when i is at the last byte of the options buffer.
intent_record.what: Added a condition `|| i == optlen - 1` to the if clause that increments i when option byte is less than 2, and reformatted the else increment expression.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds access by ensuring that when i reaches the last index, it increments i by 1 instead of attempting to read op[i+1] which would be beyond the buffer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds check to prevent out-of-bounds read in TCP option scanning when at the last byte.
intent_record.what: Extended the condition for skipping one byte in the loop from only checking if the option byte is less than 2 to also checking if the current index is the last byte of the options (i == optlen - 1).
intent_record.how: Prevents an out-of-bounds read by not accessing op[i+1] when i is at the last index. Instead, it increments i by 1, which terminates the loop.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `tcp_find_option` function at lines 46-64 contains the vulnerable loop: for (i = 0; i < optlen; ) { if (op[i] < 2) i++; else i += op[i+1]?:1; }. There is no check that i+1 is within bounds before reading op[i+1] when op[i] >= 2. If the last byte (i = optlen-1) is a non-single-byte option kind, the read of op[i+1] will be out of bounds. This matches the root cause description. No fix is present.
